title: Launch and diagnostic: why our spaces matter

standards.code_or_strand: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Michigan Health/SEL connections
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 1 — personal and shared space care

essential_question: How does taking care of my own space help me and the people I live with?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about why our spaces matter, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use age-appropriate evidence, a model, or a demonstration to communicate understanding of why our spaces matter.
Check, revise, or improve work about why our spaces matter using the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about why our spaces matter.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
materials: household-safe materials chosen and approved by the supervising adult

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “why our spaces matter.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Model one practical routine one step at a time. Name who the trusted adult is and which steps only that adult may do. Practice the safe steps, finish the whole loop, and show the routine working in one other place. Keep the explanation centered on why our spaces matter. Name the success criteria and model how to check the work.
Complete two supported examples or tasks about why our spaces matter. After each step, ask: “What tells you that step is right?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of why our spaces matter and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about why our spaces matter; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsafe step, or a weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of why our spaces matter and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about why our spaces matter; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsafe step, or a weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, the safety steps followed, the evidence of a finished loop, and the revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not score home condition, family resources, body size, or food choices. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for why our spaces matter, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain, draw, or demonstrate why the process for why our spaces matter works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of why our spaces matter, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking why our spaces matter mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, guardian confirmation, or another no-photo artifact; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible. For a real-world household task, completion evidence also requires a parent or guardian confirmation recorded through the household-authorized adult surface; a learner self-report alone does not certify an adult-supervised task.
extension: Apply why our spaces matter in a different room, at a different time of day, or with a different family member, or teach the routine to someone else with an original example. Do not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. A home, a body, a routine, or a family is never described as good, bad, clean enough, or messy.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Guardian permission is required before any real-world task begins, and the guardian chooses which tasks are appropriate for this learner and this home.
A real-world task counts as complete only when a parent or guardian confirms it. A learner self-report alone can record activity but cannot certify an adult-supervised task.
No identifiable learner photo is required. Accept a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, or guardian confirmation instead.
No dieting, calorie targets, weigh-ins, body-size scoring, earned-food framing, or food-morality language is taught, modeled, or requested.
Reflection may be kept private. No learner is required to disclose family circumstances, income, health details, faith, or personal history.
Stop and ask a trusted adult about broken glass, fire, raw-food risk, electrical hazards, heavy objects, leaks, medication, or unknown substances.
A trusted adult handles heat, stoves, ovens, sharp knives, cleaning chemicals, and appliance controls at this grade. The learner assists with safe steps only.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, labeled photograph of a finished routine, worked checklist, or adult demonstration supporting why our spaces matter.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or an adult demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For a real-world household task, record only the guardian permission and the guardian confirmation that the task was supervised and finished.
home_connection: With guardian permission, invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of why our spaces matter at home with a trusted adult nearby. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for reflecting without shame, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, guardian confirmation, or another no-photo artifact; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible. For a real-world household task, completion evidence also requires a parent or guardian confirmation recorded through the household-authorized adult surface; a learner self-report alone does not certify an adult-supervised task.
extension: Apply reflecting without shame in a different room, at a different time of day, or with a different family member, or teach the routine to someone else with an original example. Do not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. A home, a body, a routine, or a family is never described as good, bad, clean enough, or messy.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Guardian permission is required before any real-world task begins, and the guardian chooses which tasks are appropriate for this learner and this home.
A real-world task counts as complete only when a parent or guardian confirms it. A learner self-report alone can record activity but cannot certify an adult-supervised task.
No identifiable learner photo is required. Accept a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, or guardian confirmation instead.
No dieting, calorie targets, weigh-ins, body-size scoring, earned-food framing, or food-morality language is taught, modeled, or requested.
Reflection may be kept private. No learner is required to disclose family circumstances, income, health details, faith, or personal history.
Stop and ask a trusted adult about broken glass, fire, raw-food risk, electrical hazards, heavy objects, leaks, medication, or unknown substances.
A trusted adult handles heat, stoves, ovens, sharp knives, cleaning chemicals, and appliance controls at this grade. The learner assists with safe steps only.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. For a real-world household task, record only the guardian permission and the guardian confirmation that the task was supervised and finished.
home_connection: With guardian permission, invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of reflecting without shame at home with a trusted adult nearby. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
